diagram_math_checks.objects_and_maps: One real scalar input z; convolution C:R->R, C(z)=az/sigma^2; activation T:R->(-1,1), T(t)=tanh(t); affine output S:R->R, S(u)=au+b. One input/output channel and one pixel, hence all dimensions are scalar.
diagram_math_checks.relations_and_justification: The four arrows run input -> C -> T -> S -> result. Intermediate labels az/sigma^2 and tanh(az/sigma^2) match these maps. S composed with T composed with C equals a tanh(az/sigma^2)+b, exactly the Example and Network diagram prose. Since a,sigma>0, all maps are defined for every real z.

diagram_math_checks.approximation_scope: Verification 1.1 computes the prior-specific exact posterior mean D_sigma(z)=a tanh(az/sigma^2). Verification 2.1 subtracts it from the network to obtain constant error b, uniform norm |b|<eta and nonzero discrepancy at zero. The figure labels the biased output as D-tilde, preserving the distinction from exact MMSE; it asserts neither a new objective nor stationarity for the approximation.
diagram_math_checks.proof_justification: Both numbered Verification steps remain unchanged and use the finite prior/Gaussian likelihood and explicit algebra, not the diagram.
